meta.title: Open Frame Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open Frame Studio: free, open-source software for designing, documenting and exporting window and door frames — 2D editor, 3D view, frame schedule, workshop drawing and IFC export.

header.label: Window frame design
header.title: Open Frame Studio
header.tagline: Free frame software, from drawing to frame schedule
header.desc: Design windows, doors and glazed screens in 2D, check them in 3D and produce a frame schedule, workshop drawing, cutting list and IFC file from the same model. For timber, aluminium, uPVC and timber-aluminium.
header.proofModel: 2D, 3D and cutting list from one model

view3d.alt: Open Frame Studio in the dark theme: 3D view of a meranti tilt-and-turn window set in masonry, with the frame properties on the right
view3d.title: See in 3D what you draw
view3d.desc: The 3D view follows the drawing one to one: extruded profiles, glass in the rebate, sashes at their real size and the masonry around them. Mitred corners on aluminium and uPVC really are cut at 45°.

editor.alt: 2D frame editor with the dimensions of a 900 × 1400 mm tilt-and-turn window
editor.title: Draw the frame freely in 2D
editor.desc: Start from a template or an empty frame and divide it into panes. Drag dividers, place a mullion with Ctrl+click and give each pane an infill: glass, sash, door, panel or parapet. The dimension chain always adds up.

schedule.alt: Frame schedule with mark, sizes, material, glazing and Ug value per frame
schedule.title: Frame schedule and workshop drawing from the same model
schedule.desc: Every frame in a project listed with its mark, sizes, material, glazing and Ug value, as PDF and Excel. Plus A3 workshop drawings with a title block, DXF drawings with dimension lines and a cutting list that follows the drawing.

profiles.alt: Profile editor with the section of a 67 × 114 mm timber frame profile and the profile library
profiles.title: Profiles you can adjust yourself
profiles.desc: Choose from a library of profiles for timber, aluminium, uPVC and timber-aluminium, or edit a section point by point, with mirroring, snap grid and undo. Have system and supplier dimensions checked by the manufacturer.

notice.text: Try it now: open the web version and draw a frame in your browser. Nothing gets installed.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From first sketch to the workshop
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

editor.title: Free 2D editor
editor.desc: Grid subdivision, drag handles, dimension lines and infills, with hinge side, opening direction, glazing bead and hardware per pane.

templates.title: Templates
templates.desc: Tilt-and-turn window, double tilt-and-turn, sliding door, front door, door with side light and your own templates to build on.

view3d.title: 3D view
view3d.desc: Three.js preview with extruded profiles, glass in the rebate and the masonry around it.

conventions.title: Dutch drawing conventions
conventions.desc: Dimensioning to NEN 3576 and opening symbols to VKG and EN 12519 in the outside view.

ai.title: AI configurator
ai.desc: Type “Make a tilt-and-turn 900×1400” and the frame appears. Works with OpenAI, Ollama or any other compatible endpoint.

profiles.title: Profile editor
profiles.desc: Edit a profile cross-section point by point, with mirroring, snap grid and undo.

timber.title: Timber
timber.desc: KVT profiles (54, 67, 78 and 90 mm) in meranti, accoya, spruce, oak, FSC hardwood and softwood.

alu.title: Aluminium
alu.desc: Standard aluminium profiles, with 45° mitred corners.

pvc.title: uPVC
pvc.desc: Standard uPVC profiles and templates for uPVC frames.

timberAlu.title: Timber-aluminium
timberAlu.desc: Combination profiles with timber inside and aluminium outside.

cutting.title: Cutting list and joints
cutting.desc: A cutting list that follows the drawing, with joints made by the book: mortise and tenon for timber, mitres for aluminium and uPVC.

schedule.title: Frame schedule
schedule.desc: Frame schedule as PDF and Excel, with sizes, material, glazing and Ug value per frame.

workshop.title: Workshop drawing
workshop.desc: A3 workshop drawings with a title block, and DXF drawings with dimension lines for the workshop.

ifc.title: IFC export
ifc.desc: Frames as an IFC4 file for your BIM model, plus glTF for 3D. The exchange is still in development.

blender.title: Blender and Bonsai
blender.desc: Send frames straight to Blender with Bonsai for further IFC modelling.

download.label: Download
download.title: Download v0.6.0
download.lead: Free, no account needed. For Windows, macOS and Linux.
download.mobileNote: On a phone or tablet, open Open Frame Studio in the browser. For the full package, download the app on your computer.
download.betaNote: Want to try the latest development version? Beta versions for design and BIM trials are listed under the releases on GitHub.

whatsnew.label: New in v0.6
whatsnew.title: Draw freely in 2D, 3D and cutting list follow
whatsnew.desc: The 2D editor is now the source of everything: what you draw comes back one to one in the 3D view and the cutting list. The full list is in the release notes.

editor.title: Free layout
editor.desc: Switch any frame to a free layout with one button, click a pane to set its infill and place a mullion with Ctrl+click.

view3d.title: 3D follows the drawing
view3d.desc: Glass sits in the rebate, sashes have their real size and a door with side light gets masonry under the side light.

cutting.title: Cutting list matches the drawing
cutting.desc: Continuous mullions, parapet sills and, per pane, the glass, the sash and the glazing beads.

joints.title: Joints by the book
joints.desc: In timber the sills run through and the jambs are tenoned; in aluminium and uPVC the corners are mitre-welded.

symbols.title: Opening symbols in the outside view
symbols.desc: Turn, tilt and sliding symbols following the Dutch drawing convention, with the hinge side at the wide end.

settings.title: Settings are kept
settings.desc: Glazing bead, opening direction and hardware stay put after saving, switching frames and undo.

price.q: What does Open Frame Studio cost?
price.a: Nothing. Open Frame Studio is free and open source, under the CC BY-SA 4.0 licence. No subscription and no licence fees per user.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: Not to try it: open the web version in your browser. It cannot yet do everything the desktop app can. For the full package, install the app for Windows, macOS or Linux.

materials.a: Timber, aluminium, uPVC and timber-aluminium. Timber parts are tenoned, aluminium and uPVC parts are mitred, and you see that in the drawing, the 3D view and the cutting list.

bim.q: Can I use my frames in a BIM model?
bim.a: Yes. You export frames as an IFC file, or send them straight to Blender with Bonsai. The IFC exchange is still in development: check the result in your own BIM software before you build on it.

production.q: Can I use it for production right away?
production.a: Not without checking. Open Frame Studio is in development and not a validated package for manufacturer costing, compliance statements or machine control. Always check sizes, cutting lists and machining yourself before you start production.

languages.q: Which languages does the app support?
languages.a: Dutch, English and German. The drawing conventions follow Dutch practice, such as dimensioning to NEN 3576.

update.q: How do I get a new version?
update.a: The app has no automatic updater yet. Download the new installer on this page and run it.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.

core.title: Rust core
core.desc: One core (ofs-core) for the data model, the geometry and all exports: IFC, DXF, PDF, glTF, XLSX and CSV.

tauri.title: Tauri 2
tauri.desc: A thin native shell for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a small installer.

svelte.title: Svelte 5
svelte.desc: The interface, with an SVG editor for the 2D drawing.

three.title: Three.js
three.desc: The 3D view of frame, glass and masonry.

wasm.title: WebAssembly
wasm.desc: The same Rust core runs in the browser version.

ifc.title: IFC4
ifc.desc: Open exchange with BIM software, and a link with Blender and Bonsai.
